first_impression.reaction: I typed 'why do brides wear veils' on the train. The first sentence literally repeats my question and answers it. That's what I want. The Key takeaways are history facts though, not the 'why', so I'd read section 1 and probably the FAQ, then leave or bookmark.

journey.quote: Why do brides wear veils? For most couples the honest answer is a mix of history, faith, family and the simple pleasure of the moment it is lifted.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first line. Done, basically. Love that.

journey.quote: This guide follows the veil from Rome to Queen Victoria's lace, through its place in faith traditions, and on to the choices that matter now: who lifts it, whether to wear a family veil, and how a veil behaves on a windy clifftop.
journey.reaction: Tells me what's on the page. Bit long for one sentence on a phone, but fine.

journey.quote: The veil has been part of bridal dress since ancient Rome, though its look and meaning have changed many times since.
journey.reaction: Okay, but what did it mean? 'Changed many times' doesn't tell me anything. The takeaways are all trivia, none of them actually says why a bride wears one.

journey.quote: Queen Victoria wore her Honiton lace veil in 1840 thrown back over a wreath of orange blossom, not over her face, and face-covering veils came later.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that, actually interesting. I'd tell someone this.

journey.quote: For many it is about one moment: the veil lifted, and the first clear look at each other as a married couple.
journey.reaction: Heading matches my search exactly, and this is the real answer. Short section, easy.

journey.section: The wedding veil meaning in folklore
journey.quote: English folklore gives the veil one clear meaning, and it is about luck.
journey.reaction: Good for the 'wedding veil meaning' search. Clear first line, then a source link. Feels legit.

journey.section: 2. History of the wedding veil in ancient Rome
journey.quote: Her hair was arranged in six locks with woollen fillets, she wore a straight white woven tunic fastened at the waist with a "knot of Hercules", and over it all a great flame-coloured veil.
journey.reaction: This is where I'd start scrolling fast. Lots of history after this. Fine for people who want it, not me.

journey.quote: The wimple was everyday dress, not a bridal veil.
journey.reaction: So why is it here? Skipped.

journey.section: 6. Who lifts the veil, and when
journey.quote: Who lifts the veil is a choice, not a rule, and couples settle it in a few different ways.
journey.reaction: Nice bold list, scannable. This is probably my next question anyway.

journey.section: 8. Wearing a veil at a destination wedding
journey.quote: A veil that floats softly down a chapel aisle behaves very differently on a clifftop.
journey.reaction: Not what I searched, but it's a long way down so it's not in my way.

journey.quote: In Jewish tradition, it shows that the groom values the bride's inner beauty, not only her outward beauty.
journey.reaction: Good, the symbolism question answered in two lines. If I'd jumped to the FAQ I'd be happy.

journey.quote: Most brides wear it for the ceremony and portraits, then take it off for the reception.

unanswered_questions: Is there a jump list? It's nine sections plus an FAQ and on my phone that's a lot of scrolling to reach the FAQ.
Did veils ever have a 'hide the bride from evil spirits' meaning, like I've heard? The page doesn't say yes or no.

turn_offs_found.quote: The veil has been part of bridal dress since ancient Rome, though its look and meaning have changed many times since.
turn_offs_found.why: Key takeaways are the place I read first, and none of the bullets says why brides wear a veil. The intro's one-line answer (history, faith, family, the lifting moment) should be in there too.

turn_offs_found.quote: Her hair was arranged in six locks with woollen fillets, she wore a straight white woven tunic fastened at the waist with a "knot of Hercules", and over it all a great flame-coloured veil.
turn_offs_found.why: Four long history sections sit between the answer and the practical bits (lifting, FAQ). Fine on desktop, heavy on a phone with no way to skip.

would_share_with: My cousin who's deciding whether to wear one; I'd send her section 6 and the Do you have to wear a veil? bit

cta_reaction.why: I came for an answer, not to plan anything. The CTAs are soft and near the end so they didn't annoy me. I might tap the free magazine link.

top_3_changes: Make the first Key takeaways bullet the actual answer: brides wear veils for history, faith, family and the moment it is lifted, with luck as the folklore meaning.
Add a short jump list after the takeaways so phone readers can go straight to who lifts it, do you have to wear one, and the FAQ.
Trim or tuck the wimple subsection, since the page itself says it isn't a bridal veil.
